questions.stem: Which of the following are the raw materials for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through the stomata and water arrives from the roots through the xylem; these two supply all the carbon, hydrogen and oxygen in the glucose produced. Light and chlorophyll are necessary conditions rather than raw materials, because neither is used up.

distractorRationale.a: Oxygen and glucose are the products, not the raw materials
distractorRationale.c: Starch is a product and chlorophyll is a condition that is not consumed
distractorRationale.d: Nitrogen and mineral salts are needed for protein synthesis and growth, not for making glucose

questions.stem: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from the breakdown of
questions.explanation: In the light stage, energy absorbed by chlorophyll splits water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen, a reaction called photolysis. The hydrogen is used to reduce carbon dioxide in the dark stage, while the oxygen escapes as a by-product.

distractorRationale.a: Carbon dioxide is reduced and its carbon and oxygen end up in the glucose
distractorRationale.c: Glucose is a product of photosynthesis, not a source of the oxygen released
distractorRationale.d: Chlorophyll absorbs light and is not broken down

questions.stem: Why must a plant be kept in complete darkness for 48 hours before an experiment on the necessity of light for starch formation?

options.text: To make the leaves softer for testing
To remove all the starch already stored in the leaves
To increase the amount of chlorophyll in the leaves
To close all the stomata permanently

questions.explanation: In darkness the plant continues to respire and uses up its stored starch, so the leaves become destarched. Without this step, starch detected at the end of the experiment might simply be starch that was present before the experiment began, and the result would prove nothing.

distractorRationale.a: Leaves are softened later by boiling and dipping in warm water, not by darkness
distractorRationale.c: Chlorophyll does not increase in darkness; leaves kept dark eventually turn pale
distractorRationale.d: Stomata close in darkness but reopen in light, and this is not the purpose of the step

questions.stem: A destarched leaf is partly covered with black paper and the plant left in sunlight for six hours. After decolourising and testing with iodine solution, the result will be that the

options.text: covered part turns blue-black and the exposed part stays brown
exposed part turns blue-black and the covered part stays brown

questions.explanation: Only the exposed part received light, so only there could photosynthesis occur and starch accumulate; iodine turns blue-black in the presence of starch. The covered part, lacking light, made no starch and so keeps the brown colour of the iodine solution.

distractorRationale.a: This reverses the result; the covered part received no light and could not make starch
distractorRationale.c: The covered part had no light, so it cannot contain starch
distractorRationale.d: The exposed part had light, water and carbon dioxide, so starch must have formed there

questions.stem: Which statement about the dark stage of photosynthesis is correct?

options.text: It takes place in the stroma and uses hydrogen and ATP produced in the light stage
It splits water to release oxygen
It requires chlorophyll to absorb light directly

questions.explanation: The dark stage is better called light-independent: it happens in the stroma of the chloroplast and does not need light itself, but it consumes the hydrogen and ATP that the light stage supplies. That dependence is why it soon stops once the light goes out, and it runs perfectly well in daylight.

distractorRationale.a: The name refers to independence from light, not to night time; it runs during the day too
distractorRationale.c: Photolysis of water is the defining event of the light stage
distractorRationale.d: Direct light absorption by chlorophyll belongs to the light stage

questions.stem: A water plant is illuminated brightly at 25 °C in water containing plenty of dissolved carbon dioxide, and bubbles are counted. When the light intensity is doubled the bubble rate does not increase. The most likely limiting factor is now

options.text: the amount of oxygen in the water

questions.explanation: If doubling the light produces no extra oxygen, light can no longer be the factor in shortest supply. Something else must now be capping the rate, and of the remaining candidates only carbon dioxide supply or temperature, which controls enzyme activity, can play that role.

distractorRationale.a: Light has been ruled out precisely because increasing it changed nothing
distractorRationale.c: The plant is submerged, so water is in unlimited supply
distractorRationale.d: Oxygen is a product; a build-up of product is not treated as a limiting factor here

questions.stem: Most of the photosynthesis in a leaf takes place in the
questions.explanation: Palisade cells sit directly beneath the transparent upper epidermis, are elongated so that many can be packed side by side, and contain far more chloroplasts than any other leaf cell. Being first in the path of the light makes them the main site of photosynthesis.

distractorRationale.a: The cuticle is a non-living waxy layer with no chloroplasts
distractorRationale.c: Xylem vessels are dead, hollow tubes that transport water
distractorRationale.d: Guard cells do contain a few chloroplasts, but they are far too few to account for most of the leaf's output

questions.stem: A leaf must be boiled in ethanol before the iodine test in order to remove the chlorophyll so that the colour change can be seen.
questions.explanation: True. Chlorophyll dissolves in hot ethanol, leaving the leaf almost white so that a blue-black colour is clearly visible. Because ethanol is highly flammable it must be heated in a water bath rather than over a naked flame.

questions.stem: A variegated leaf with green and white patches is destarched, exposed to sunlight and then tested with iodine. Which conclusion can be drawn from the result?

options.text: Only the green patches turn blue-black, showing that chlorophyll is necessary for photosynthesis
Only the white patches turn blue-black, showing that chlorophyll blocks photosynthesis
The whole leaf turns blue-black, showing that light alone is sufficient
No part turns blue-black, showing that variegated leaves cannot photosynthesise

questions.explanation: Both regions of the same leaf received identical light, carbon dioxide, water and temperature, so chlorophyll is the only variable. Starch forming only where chlorophyll is present shows that chlorophyll is necessary, which is why a variegated leaf is the standard experiment for this purpose.

distractorRationale.b: The white patches have no chlorophyll to trap light energy, so they cannot make starch
distractorRationale.c: If light alone were sufficient the white patches would also make starch, which they do not
distractorRationale.d: The green patches do photosynthesise normally

questions.stem: Write the balanced equation for photosynthesis and explain three ways in which the structure of a leaf makes it efficient at carrying out the process.
markingGuide: Balanced equation correct, including light and chlorophyll shown over the arrow: 6CO2 + 6H2O gives C6H12O6 + 6O2 (3 marks)
Adaptation 1: broad, flat lamina provides a large surface area to absorb the maximum amount of light (2 marks)
Adaptation 2: the leaf is thin, and the spongy mesophyll contains air spaces, so carbon dioxide diffuses rapidly to every cell (2 marks)
Adaptation 3: palisade cells packed with chloroplasts lie just beneath a transparent epidermis and cuticle, so light reaches the chlorophyll with least obstruction (2 marks)
Accept also: numerous stomata for gaseous exchange; a network of veins delivering water and removing sugar (1 mark each if used in place of the above)
questions.explanation: The equation must balance and should show light and chlorophyll as conditions above the arrow rather than as reactants. Each adaptation should be stated together with the advantage it gives, since a bare list of leaf parts does not show understanding.
